title: Evident Insights: The Evident AI Index for Insurance and Insurance AI Coverage
answer: Evident Insights publishes the Evident AI Index for Insurance, a benchmark of 30 large North American and European insurers on AI talent, innovation, executive leadership and governance. Its 2026 edition ranks Allianz first, ahead of last year's leader AXA, with Manulife third and Zurich the biggest climber. Evident's newsletters also report how insurers are deploying AI, including Allianz's multi-agent claims system and AXA's weather risk platform.

sections.body: Evident Insights publishes the Evident AI Index and a Banking Brief newsletter, alongside recaps of its Evident AI Symposium events. The insurance material sits mainly in a newsletter article reporting the release of the 2026 Evident AI Index for Insurance, which assesses 30 of the largest insurance companies across North America and Europe. The site also carries banking-focused editions that touch on insurance-adjacent themes such as AI talent, governance and cost. The pages read were published between November 2024 and 2026, with the insurance index article dated to the 2026 release week.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The 2026 Evident AI Index for Insurance assesses 30 of the largest insurers in North America and Europe on the quality of their AI talent stack, the impacts of their innovation efforts, the tech leadership of their C-suites and the measures they have put in place to govern and scale AI effectively. Allianz leads on AI maturity, leapfrogging AXA, last year's top finisher. Manulife climbs to third and is again the top life insurer, while Zurich rises eight places, more than any other ranked firm, to fourth. Liberty Mutual jumps two places to become the top property and casualty insurer on AI. More than 40% of the AI tools released in 2026 by the 30 tracked insurers automate several steps of a workflow rather than a single task. Allianz's Project Nemo, a multi-agent system handling claims steps from validating coverage to checking fraud, cut processing time on some food spoilage claims from days to hours. AXA's extreme weather risk platform turns real-time data into predictive insights for proactive disaster prevention. Manulife's Singapore sales support agent, which recommends actions and drafts personal notes, produced a 5% higher repurchase rate in pilot.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The Index covers 30 insurers across North America and Europe. Allianz ranks first, AXA second, Manulife third and Zurich fourth after rising eight places, with Liberty Mutual the top property and casualty insurer. More than 40% of AI tools released in 2026 by the tracked insurers automate several workflow steps. Project Nemo cut some food spoilage claims from days to hours. Manulife's sales agent pilot produced a 5% higher repurchase rate. Allianz CFO Claire-Marie Coste-Lepoutre said productivity becomes a by-product of optimized processes that can be reinjected into pricing. AXA CEO Thomas Buberl said AI is an efficiency play but not only, and will change how customers access insurance, product personalization and customer experience.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in insurance, this is the sector's comparative maturity scoreboard. It names which insurers lead on AI talent, innovation, leadership and governance, and shows movement year on year, such as Allianz overtaking AXA and Zurich's eight-place climb. The accompanying detail on Project Nemo, AXA's weather platform and Manulife's sales agent gives concrete examples of AI moving from single-task tools to multi-step workflows. The executive quotes frame AI as both an efficiency play and a route to changed customer experience and pricing, which is useful context for anyone tracking how insurers justify AI investment.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Insurance

sections.body: The insurance coverage is concentrated in a single newsletter article about the 2026 Index release, with the rest of the site's pages read focused on banking, events and AI cost management. The Index itself is described as covering 30 large insurers in North America and Europe, so it does not represent the global industry or smaller carriers. The article reports rankings and examples rather than the full methodology, and the site is published by the index provider, so the material is promotional in part.
